questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Both academic opportunities, career opportunities, personal connection to the destination and explore new cultures meant a lot to me. Most important it was to study more music business related courses as these don't exist at university level in Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed my time and stayed in London with family which was very important to me.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult but I let people know that I was new and their student coordinator Francoise was a big help

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Student coordinators (Francoise was a big help to me)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was one intro meeting - besides that I had to let the teacher know I was and exchange student because I didn't know anything about their grading systemt, online systems (moodle) and so on.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived with family so very easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend it. I thought Kent/Canterbury was a bit too boring and you can live in a big city or other exciting places for the same price. Especially if you only have 2 days with courses like me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 1000 for the cheapest room is not okay I think

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy, it was just personal information that you had to fill out.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy, it was just personal information that you had to fill out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Their student coordinators will help you with everything!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Semi. The one I signed up for clashed with another course of mine but I luckily just found another one!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Patience. You might get tour timetable the same week as classes start.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was well planned.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the course were very easy which helped as I didn't know much about the subjects.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Easier to understand and less stressfull. I think sometimes, loads of people experience burnouts at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Sex Gender and Performance
- Music Journalism, PRESS and PR
- Music Marketing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If in the music aspect, definitely - Music Journalism, PRESS and PR
- Music Marketing. Or courses with Ben Horner who is an amazing teacher

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any unexpected costs and I lived off campus, but I do think that housing is more expensive than Denmark but food is cheaper.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Train tickets were more expensive than I thought but luckily I lived for free with family.
Food and eating out is less expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't live on campus but there seemed to be many non academic opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, fitness and social gatherings. Like yoga with dogs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Meet up with other danish people or meet up with people that have the same activity of preference as you

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: London! Or the costs like Bath, Cornwall, Brighton and so on

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as I do have family there. I can though be very tiring to talk english all the time but if you are lucky there will be other exchange students as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go out and meet people. Others might be in the same boat as you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing else than that people in university in the uk are much younger than the average age in denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the pubs!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make an effort in getting to know people on and off campus

Go explore elsewhere than Kent

Let people know that you are an exchange student and that you are new.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't have to stay or live in Kent. Try to get out of Canterbury as it is easy to just hang around campus. The UK is huge so make your stay worth the time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to study courses that wasn't available in Denmark!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The transport. I lived in London and it was 4-5 hours travel but luckily only twice a week. It was expensive but I was productive on my train ride.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
